## Findings
- claim-1: The recorded two families are \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) and \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\), where \(a=\min(q-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\), with \(q=n-r\). [source-6@L18-L42|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-2: The requested standalone integral transpose-reduction lemma is established: it identifies the theorem-displayed first family at \((r,q;i,j)\) with the Remark 4.7 second family at \((q,r;j,i)\), descends to Grassmannian quotients, and preserves minimality.
## Strategy
Let \(\Lambda\) be the integral symmetric-function ring and \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\). Since
\[
\lambda\subseteq q^r\iff\lambda'\subseteq r^q,
\]
\(\omega(I_{r,q})=I_{q,r}\). Hence it descends to an integral graded-ring isomorphism
\[
\bar\omega_{r,q}:\Lambda/I_{r,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda/I_{q,r}.
\]

Define
\[
J_{r,q;i,j}:=\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda .
\]
Basiswise,
\[
i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq q^r
\iff
j^i\subseteq\lambda'\subseteq r^q,
\]
so
\[
\bar\omega_{r,q}(J_{r,q;i,j})=J_{q,r;j,i}.
\]

For bigrassmannian data \((r,s,t,n)\), put \(q=n-r\) and
\[
(r',s',t',n')=(q,n-s,q-s+t,n).
\]
Then
\[
i'=s'-t'+1=j,\qquad j'=r'-t'+1=i.
\]
Admissibility holds: \(t'\le q\) follows from \(t\le s\), \(t'\le n-s\) from \(t\le r\), and
\[
t'=q-s+t>q-s=r'+s'-n'
\]
from \(t>r+s-n=s-q\); integrality gives \(t'\ge1\).

Moreover,
\[
a'=\min(r-j,q-i)=a,\qquad b'=\min(j,i)=b.
\]
The theorem family at transformed parameters is
\[
\{\bar s_\mu:j^i\subseteq\mu\subseteq(j^i,b^a)\}.
\]
Transposition sends its upper bound to
\[
(j^i,b^a)'=((i+a)^b,i^{j-b}),
\]
and therefore sends this family exactly to
\[
\{\bar s_\nu:i^j\subseteq\nu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\},
\]
the Remark 4.7 family. The theorem/Remark distinction is source-grounded in [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 95-110] and [lines 503-512].

Finally, a ring isomorphism preserves generation and proper containment of subfamilies. Thus a family is minimal in \(J_{q,r;j,i}\) iff its transpose is minimal in \(J_{r,q;i,j}\).

Accordingly, the requested transpose-reduction lemma is established.
